state.claim: Officer who wore Trump 2020 mask to polls to face disciplinary action

records.title: Miami Cop Pictured in Uniform at Polling Site With Trump Mask
records.retrieval_query: What primary records or official statements confirm that an officer wore a Trump 2020 mask at a polling place?

passages.P1: A Miami police officer faces disciplinary action after he went to an early-voting polling site in uniform while also wearing a Trump 2020 face mask.
passages.P2: The officer, identified as Daniel Ubeda, was photographed wearing full uniform at the Government Center in Miami.
passages.P3: He had a police badge, gun, and a name tag that says "Ubeda." His mask said "Trump 2020: No more bulls---".
passages.P4: The photo at the polling site was taken and tweeted on Tuesday by Steve Simeonidis, the chairman of the Miami-Dade Democratic Party.
passages.P5: In his tweet, Simeonidis said Ubeda's action was "city-funded voter intimidation" and called for his suspension from the police force.
passages.P7: Simeonidis later told the Miami Herald that Ubeda had "laughed it off" when he was questioned about the mask.
passages.P8: Florida law forbids any "officer or employer of the state" from using their authority to interfere with an election or coerce or intimidate people into voting for a particular political party.
passages.P9: State law also prevents people campaigning for a particular candidate from being within 150 feet from polling sites. Simeonidis told the Herald that Ubeda was "well within" that distance.
passages.P10: The Miami Police Department and city authorities did not name the officer, but confirmed that the man photographed was one of their officers. They said he would be disciplined, but did not specify how.
passages.P11: In a statement to CBS Miami Miami Police Chief Jorge Colina said: "We are aware of the photograph being circulated of a Miami Police officer wearing a political mask in uniform.
passages.P12: "This behavior is unacceptable, a violation of departmental policy, and is being addressed immediately."
passages.P13: Deputy Police Chief Ron Papier told the Herald that the department would take "appropriate disciplinary action" against Ubeda. He said "the mask has offensive language, which is also a violation of department policy."
passages.P14: Mayor Francis Suarez of Miami told reporters on Tuesday that the photo was taken while the officer was in line to cast his own vote. He condemned his actions and said he would be disciplined.
passages.P15: "The City of Miami and the Miami Police Department do not support or endorse any candidate for a political party or elected office. The involved officer was not authorized to wear a mask with political messaging, nor was he given any administrative direction to support a political candidate or political party," Suarez said.
passages.P16: "His actions have violated departmental policy and he will be disciplined."
passages.P17: Suarez also called the officer's actions "unacceptable" and "something that we cannot condone and we do not accept."
passages.P18: Business Insider has contacted the Trump campaign for comment.
passages.P19: The president has for months personally encouraged his supporters to go to polling places around the country and monitor votes being counted.

passages.P2: # Miami PD to Discipline Officer Photographed Wearing Pro-Trump Mask at Polling Location
passages.P3: ## The police officer in the picture, whose name tag identifies them as Officer Ubeda, can be seen wearing a "Trump 2020' face mask
passages.P4: #### Published October 20, 2020 • Updated on October 21, 2020 at 1:21 pm
passages.P6: A picture of a Miami police officer wearing a Trump 2020 mask at a polling site was posted on social media and quickly stirred up controversy. NBC 6’s Steve Litz reports.
passages.P7: City of Miami Police say they will discipline a police officer who was photographed wearing a Trump face mask while in uniform at an early voting polling location Tuesday morning.
passages.P8: The photo was tweeted by Steve Simeonidis, Chair of Miami-Dade Democrats, inside the Stephen P. Clark Government Center in Downtown Miami. In his Tweet, Simeonidis calls the officer's mask a form of "voter intimidation".
passages.P9: The police officer in the picture, whose name tag identifies them as Officer Ubeda, can be seen wearing a "Trump 2020' face mask.
passages.P11: In a statement, City of Miami Police said they were aware of the photograph, calling the officer's behavior unacceptable.
passages.P12: "This behavior is unacceptable, a violation of departmental policy, and is being addressed immediately," City of Miami Police said.
passages.P13: City of Miami Mayor Francis Suarez said the officer would be disciplined.
passages.P19: "It's inappropriate," Suarez said. "A police officer is supposed to be impartial, irrespective who the person was, whatever sign it is."
passages.P20: The mayor added that the officer was in the polling location to vote, but it was unclear if the officer was on duty.
passages.P21: Miami Police did not explain what discipline the officer would face, but Suarez said had he not been voting, the repercussions could have been much worse.
passages.P22: In a statement, the Fraternal Order of Police said the officer was protected under Florida law which allows officers to vote in uniform.
passages.P23: However, the organization did not comment on Miami Police Department's policy on wearing political masks. Instead, the FOP stated that it has endorsed President Trump for reelection.
